chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, he said:
When you are summoned to the testimony, then answer.

key_terms.الشهادة: Testimony, witnessing; the act of bearing witness in legal or religious matters
key_terms.دُعِيتَ: You are summoned/called; the passive form emphasizes the formal legal nature of the summons
key_terms.فَأَجِبْ: Then answer/respond; the imperative form indicates obligation

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to respond when called to give testimony in Islam?
ai.summary: The Imam (peace be upon him) through the chain reaching Jarrah al-Mada'ini declares that it is obligatory to respond when called upon to give testimony. This hadith establishes a fundamental rule of Islamic jurisprudence regarding the duty of witnessing: when a Muslim is called to testify, they must respond to that summons. This ruling reflects the Islamic understanding that testimony is a collective religious duty (fard kifaya or fard 'ayn), not merely a personal choice, as it is essential for the preservation of rights and justice in the community.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘
When you are summoned to the testimony, so answer’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Madi’iniy who has narrated the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you are called to present your testimony you must accept to testify.’”
